script.text: This clip tells a stranger my name. My building. And my phone number.
script.on_screen: c2 input playing full-bleed; notification 'Rohan Kulkarni' and gold 'KULKARNI — 12' visible; kinetic words NAME / BUILDING / NUMBER

script.text: All fictional. But creators post clips like this every day.
script.on_screen: Caption chip: 'fictional data · composited clip'

script.text: A name on a parcel. A society board behind you. A number you say out loud.
script.on_screen: Three quick crops from c1/c2/c3: label, board, waveform

script.text: Most redaction tools look for a fixed list. Faces. License plates. Screens. Documents.
script.on_screen: Kinetic list of four classes, each ticking off

script.text: On my held-out clips, that list found zero of four planted leaks.
script.on_screen: Big stat card: 0 / 4

script.text: So Veil asks a different question. What, in this video, could identify you?
script.on_screen: Cut to Veil UI (c2), floating window

script.text: Muse Spark looks at keyframes and proposes candidates, each with a reason. The notification shows a full name. The gold plate shows a surname and a flat number.
script.on_screen: Zoom on amber Spark boxes + callouts with 'why' text from manifest

script.text: None of these is a face or a license plate. The model has to understand the scene.
script.on_screen: Hold on callouts; small grey 'baseline: face · plate' chips with no box on the name

script.text: SAM 3.1 tracks each one through every frame. And the output covers exactly those regions.
script.on_screen: Scrub slider 6s→12s; output pane shows covers following; timeline bars

script.text: With Spark in the loop, three of four planted leaks were found. The delivery-box label was still missed.
script.on_screen: Stat card: 0/4 → 3/4, small line 'missed: delivery-box label'

script.text: Then code checks the work. Veil decodes its own output and confirms the covers are really there.
script.on_screen: Findings rows: 'cover verified in decoded output on all 557 masked frames'

script.text: It re-reads the output with local OCR, and runs a face detector on sampled frames.
script.on_screen: Checks listed panel: RAN rows

script.text: And models make mistakes. Here, SAM put the name mask on a block of code.
script.on_screen: Zoom on Mask check table: REJECTED row

script.text: Local OCR read the mask, found code instead of the name Spark claimed, and threw it out.
script.on_screen: Highlight OCR text 'def total(items)' vs claimed 'KULKARNI'

script.text: Spoken numbers too. Muse Voice Transcribe hears a phone number read out in Hindi, and Veil mutes it.
script.on_screen: c3 UI (?run=c3): transcript in Devanagari, red mute bar on timeline

script.text: Then it transcribes the output again. No digit run left.
script.on_screen: Findings row: 're-transcription of the output found no phone-like digit run'

script.text: But the transcript gets digits wrong, and the mute window is still wider than my own limit.
script.on_screen: Callout on garbled digits; small card 'over-cover 2.85 s · limit 2.5 s'

script.text: That's the point. Veil never says a video is safe.
script.on_screen: Headline panel: 'unresolved finding(s). Review them before sharing.'

script.text: Every item is covered, unresolved, or not checked. And it tells you why.
script.on_screen: Findings table: COVERED / UNRESOLVED / NOT_CHECKED rows with reasons

script.text: In this clip, two items are unresolved. Eight weren't checked, because a model call failed or they hit my cost cap.
script.on_screen: Zoom: UNRESOLVED rows (red) and NOT_CHECKED rows (amber) with reasons

script.text: I held myself to that too. I wrote a test gate before running it. It failed. I fixed two narrow failures afterwards, labelled as post-gate. One still fails.
script.on_screen: GATE_RESULT.md FAIL table → post-gate table (G2 PASS post-gate, G4b FAIL)

script.text: Run it on a clip, read the receipt, and decide before you post.
script.on_screen: Terminal: 'veil run clip.mp4 --run-id demo' then receipt

script.text: Models propose. Code decides. Veil. Built solo, with Muse Spark, SAM 3.1, and Muse Voice.
script.on_screen: Outro: Veil wordmark, three model chips, repo URL, footage attribution
